title: Savory Cottage Cheese Breakfast Bowls
subtitle: A fast, no-cook breakfast bowl built on cottage cheese, cucumber, tomato, and everything seasoning.
description: Cottage cheese is topped with diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, avocado, and an everything-bagel seasoning for a savory, no-cook breakfast. It is built for mornings when nobody wants to fire up the stove but still wants real protein.

steps.title: Prep the line
steps.instruction: Dice cucumber and avocado, halve cherry tomatoes, and set cottage cheese and each topping out in separate bowls so the crew can build their own without cross-contamination.

steps.title: Build order
steps.instruction: Scoop cottage cheese into a bowl first, then top with cucumber, tomatoes, and avocado. Finish with everything seasoning and a light drizzle of olive oil.

steps.title: Hold briefly
steps.instruction: This bowl holds about 20 minutes covered in the fridge before the cucumber and tomato start releasing water — build close to serving time when possible.

steps.title: Serve cold
steps.instruction: Serve cold with hot sauce on the side for anyone who wants heat. This is a fast, no-stove option when the hall is busy.

stationWorkflow: Set out cottage cheese and all toppings in separate bowls for a self-serve build.
Keep tomatoes and cucumber cold until the moment of assembly so bowls don't get watery.
Have everything seasoning and hot sauce within reach at the end of the line.
cleanupNotes: Rinse the cutting board right after dicing vegetables — no cooked residue to worry about, but keep raw-produce boards separate from any meat prep that day.
Store unused toppings back in the fridge immediately rather than leaving them out.
leftovers: Best assembled fresh — store cottage cheese and toppings separately if planning ahead.
Cottage cheese itself keeps up to a week; diced vegetables are best used within 2 days.
